as ''Asociația Club Sportiv Municipal Politehnica Iași'' | dissolved = {{start date and age|df=yes|14 July 2026}} | ground = [[Emil Alexandrescu Stadium|Emil Alexandrescu]] | capacity = 11,390 | owntitle = Owner | owner = | chairman = | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = | league = | season = [[2025–26 Liga II|2025–26]] | position = Liga II, 12th of 22 }} '''Fotbal Club Politehnica Iași''' ({{IPA|ro|po.liˈteh.nika ˈjaʃʲ}}), commonly known as '''Politehnica Iași''' or simply '''Poli Iași''', was a Romanian professional [[Association football|football]] club based in the city of [[Iași]], [[Iași County]]. Named after the [[Gheorghe Asachi Technical University of Iași]], the original team was founded in 1945 and played in blue and white at the [[Stadionul Emil Alexandrescu]] until its dissolution in 2010. Later that year, a new entity was formed under the name [[FC Politehnica Iași (2010)|ACSMU Politehnica Iași]], following a merger between [[Tricolorul Breaza]] and ''Navobi Iași''. The new club began directly in the [[Liga II]] and is regarded as the historical successor of the original team, buying at auction its colours, history, and records. Between 2011 and 2016, it was known as ''CSM Studențesc Iași'', before reverting to the name Politehnica Iași. It debuted in the [[Liga I]] during the [[2012–13 Liga I|2012–13 season]] and equalled its all-time best finish by placing sixth in the [[2017–18 Liga I|2017–18 season]]. Politehnica Iași currently plays in the [[Liga II]], wearing white and blue [[Kit (association football)|kits]], and hosts matches at the 11,390-capacity [[Stadionul Emil Alexandrescu]], built in 1960."}}
